_readme: One line per row you have ruled on: the row id mapped to true when the TEXT explicitly attributes the cuts to AI, false when it does not. Rows you leave out stay UNADJUDICATED and are scored nowhere -- nothing here is ever defaulted. The rows waiting for you are in ai-causation-2026-08.review.md. When you are done, run `python3 railway/ab_ai_causation.py --rescore`: it folds your calls in, calls no model and spends nothing, so acting on this file is free.

_what_these_are: A Claude session on 2026-08-19 applied the WRITTEN rubric (extractor.ai_causation_prompt + finalize_ai_causation + methodology page #m-ai + the alt_allowed_ai_causation 'ai_linked' definition) to the stored text of each of the 34 open rows. No model was asked to break a tie and no model vote was consulted. But a rubric APPLIED BY A MODEL is still a model's reading, and this gold set exists precisely because model consensus cannot stand in for truth. These are a reading, not a judgement.
_how_to_confirm: Read docs/recall-reference-sets/ai-causation-2026-08.recommendations.md (one line per row: deciding phrase, ruling, rubric reason). To CONFIRM a row, strip its `rec:` prefix -- `"rec:70293": true` becomes `"70293": true` -- and it becomes a gold label on the next --rescore. To DISAGREE, flip its true/false before stripping. To send a row back to UNADJUDICATED, delete the line. Confirm the lot in one edit: `sed -i '' 's/"rec:/"/' docs/recall-reference-sets/ai-causation-2026-08.adjudications.json`. Then set _confirmed_by to your name and run `python3 railway/ab_ai_causation.py --rescore`.

_left_for_the_owner: 107375 (General Motors) is still deliberately absent, and the speaker ruling does NOT settle it. GM cut IT staff in order to re-hire people with stronger AI skills, so no worker was replaced by a machine and the open question is whether an 'AI skills swap' is AI causing the cuts at all. That question survives the speaker ruling, which is why this row is scored nowhere. (On speaker alone it would fail anyway: the attribution was the press's, GM's own statement named no AI.)
_class_flag: 107481 and 107491 -- and 107375, which is not even recommended -- all turn on ONE question: does ai_explicit require the EMPLOYER to name AI, or does an explicit causal statement in the source text suffice whoever made it? These rulings assume the latter, because alt_allowed_ai_causation() puts 'the company or press' on the LOOSE side of ai_linked, so the split is looseness, not speaker. THE OWNER IS BEING ASKED THIS DIRECTLY; do not resolve it here. If he rules 'the employer must say it', flip rec:107481 and rec:107491 to false as a class and leave 107375 out. If he rules 'the source text suffices', confirm them as they stand and 107375 still needs its own answer (see the recommendations file).
_the_ruling: THE SPEAKER QUESTION IS ANSWERED. ai_explicit requires THE EMPLOYER to have attributed the cuts to AI. A report counts when it quotes or reports the employer saying it. A journalist's own characterisation, with no such statement from the employer, is the BROAD tier ('ai_linked'), not this one. The rule is now stated for readers on the methodology page (#m-ai), asked for in extractor.ai_causation_prompt() and SYSTEM_PROMPT rule 2, and described in alt_allowed_ai_causation(). It is no longer derived across three files and stated in none.

They are NOT confirmed, because five of them (70293, 70653, 54973, 48830, 70683) are stored LIVE as ai_explicit=1, so confirming them adds five rows to the corrections worklist for the number this product is named after. That is the owner's call, not a session's. Strip the six prefixes to accept, or flip a value first to disagree.
